A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MolFLAE. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and matchable despite changes in terminology, pagination, and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecule-generation benchmarks, molecule-editing and interpolation results, QM9 ablations, and computational optimization of human glucocorticoid receptor ligands.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds editing-quality measurements, GEOM-Drugs drug-likeness comparisons, and a reported one-step-decoder experiment.

M1.justification: The stated posterior parameterization changes from Linear([z_x, z_h]) to Linear(z_h) in Equations 4 and 12. Algorithm 2 also explicitly sets mu_x = z_x. This is a limited correction to the specified procedure; the virtual-node encoder, VAE objectives, and BFN decoder remain. Implementation changes or retraining are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM9, GEOM-Drugs, and ZINC-9M for the same generation and manipulation tasks, alongside the same receptor-optimization case study. The added measurements and decoder ablation do not introduce different data coverage or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators. New Table 7 evaluates the already-compared EDM, GeoLDM, and UniGEM on additional GEOM-Drugs metrics. GeoBFN is explicitly excluded from this new comparison because checkpoints were unavailable, but remains in the original benchmark; no comparator is removed from a corresponding existing comparison.

E3.justification: v2 extends editing evaluations with validity and atom-stability metrics. New Appendix E specifies a drug-likeness evaluation using 10,000 samples per model, default settings, OpenBabel bond inference, Schrodinger bond-order correction, and RDKit evaluation. Original splits, training settings, and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds an attempted one-step-decoder ablation, reporting no valid molecules. New Table 6 examines validity and atom stability along interpolation trajectories. The original regularization, latent-dimension, and virtual-node-count ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same Pearson correlations, p-values, and 5% significance criterion for interpolation. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures; its new tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Retained experimental scores are unchanged, but v2 substantially extends findings on molecular quality through Tables 2, 3, 6, and 7. Interpolation validity is newly reported as 99.8-100%. New Table 7 reports MolFLAE QED 0.60 and strain energy 84.66, versus GeoLDM 0.40 and 446.1. Appendix F adds the failed one-step-decoding outcome. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces the SE(3) group definition with E(3), allowing orthogonal transformations including reflections, and revises Proposition A.1 accordingly. It also explains the subgroup relationship. This changes the formal symmetry scope, while the remaining derivations are retained and no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion now characterize the latent space as E(3)-equivariant, explicitly encompassing reflections. Appendix A.2 presents this as a more accurate characterization of the network. The central claims about fixed-dimensional representations, zero-shot manipulation, and competitive generation remain.

C2.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E newly interpret the drug-likeness results as supporting structurally reasonable, drug-like generation. Appendix F adds a practical qualification concerning the unsuccessful one-step simplification. The existing partial-disentanglement interpretation and associated future-work limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, definitions of previously reported generation metrics in Appendix D, and processing instructions for the new drug-likeness evaluation. The hardware, training costs, splits, and hyperparameter tables are unchanged apart from numbering.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds UniMoMo and expands its discussion of block-based latent representations, explicitly discussing PepGLAD and limitations for interpolation and reuse in autoregressive modeling. PepGLAD was already cited in v1. The broader positioning against variable-length and non-equivariant representations remains.

P1.justification: v2 updates equivariance terminology, corrects several wording and notation errors, expands related-work and metric explanations, and inserts a drug-likeness appendix. Author/contact and conference information also change. The overall narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 gain validity and atom-stability rows or columns, and Tables 6 and 7 are new displays. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and the document reflows. All six original figures retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for molecule manipulation through validity and atom-stability checks and adds useful drug-likeness and strain-energy comparisons. The posterior equations and algorithm become more consistent, while the code link and processing details improve reproducibility information. These targeted gains improve the retained study, although the new results lack uncertainty estimates and the one-step experiment remains sparsely documented.
